opportunities.summary: The current call is closed because it reached the cap of 800 applications. The next call opens on 15 November 2026 and feeds the July 2027 selection meeting. There is no fixed deadline: since 2026 each call closes as soon as 800 applications come in, so applicants should submit on or right after opening day. A draft can be saved in the portal now. Calls open three times a year, on 15 March, 15 July and 15 November. Carlos appears eligible. He is a Spanish national who has not lived in Germany, so the 90-days-in-the-last-18-months rule should not affect him as long as his Copenhagen visit and other stays were outside Germany. His expected PhD date (March 2027) falls before the July 2027 selection meeting, which the rules allow if he submits a written summary of his thesis findings. Strong host options include Brouwer and von Oppen (FU Berlin) and Hassler (RWTH Aachen). His doctoral supervisor cannot be the host.
opportunities.eligibility: Non-German researchers with a doctorate completed within the last 4 years, or completed before the selection meeting (with a written summary of findings). Mothers get up to 2 extra years per child, capped at 6 years. Applicants must not have spent more than 90 days in Germany in the 18 months before applying, nor been funded from German sources or done doctoral work in Germany during that time. German nationals and people educated in Germany are eligible only after more than 10 years abroad (or more than 5 years with strong ties to their country of residence). Former Humboldt fellows or award winners cannot apply. Applications are submitted directly by the researcher, together with a mentoring agreement from the host.
opportunities.duration: 6–24 months for postdocs, which can be split into up to 3 stays within 3 years. Each stay lasts at least 6 months, or two 3-month blocks. An optional 2–4-month German language course before the stay does not count toward this.
opportunities.salary: €3,000 per month for postdocs, plus a family allowance, a subsidy for private health insurance and a travel allowance. The host institute receives €800 per month for natural sciences. Expected success rate is 20–25%.

opportunities.summary: No call is open today (2026-11-04). The 2026 call (HORIZON-MSCA-2026-PF-01) ran from 9 April to 9 September 2026, with results due around February 2027. The next call, HORIZON-MSCA-2027-PF-01-01, is listed as forthcoming on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and the MSCA site: planned opening 7 April 2027, deadline 8 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. Some sources still mark these dates as provisional, so check the portal before relying on them. European Fellowships last 12–24 months at a host in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. They pay the researcher living, mobility and, where applicable, family allowances, and pay the host research, training, networking, management and indirect costs. The host PI/organisation writes the proposal with the fellow, submits it, and if funded employs and supervises the fellow. Carlos appears eligible for the 2027 call. His PhD (expected March 2027) would be awarded before the September 2027 deadline, he is well within the 8-year limit, and he has lived only in Spain. That means any host outside Spain (for example Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Sweden or Switzerland) meets the mobility rule. A Spanish host would not. Because his 2025 Copenhagen visit was short, Denmark should still be fine as a host. As an EU national he could also apply for a Global Fellowship to the US or Canada, which adds a mandatory 12-month return phase in Europe. Host institutions often set internal deadlines between April and July, so he should contact host PIs early in 2027.
opportunities.eligibility: Any nationality (European Fellowships). You need a PhD by the call deadline; a defended thesis counts even before the degree is formally awarded. You can have at most 8 years of research experience after the PhD; career breaks, work outside research, parental leave and long sick leave are not counted. Mobility rule: in the 36 months before the deadline, you must not have lived or had your main activity (work, studies) in the host country for more than 12 months. From 2026, a proposal that scored below 80% the year before cannot be resubmitted with the same host and researcher. Global Fellowships are open only to EU nationals or long-term residents.
opportunities.duration: 12–24 months (European Fellowships). Global Fellowships are 24–36 months: 12–24 months outside Europe plus a mandatory 12-month return phase. An optional non-academic placement of up to 6 months is possible at the end.
opportunities.salary: Unit-cost funding. The researcher receives a living allowance (adjusted by the host country's correction coefficient), a mobility allowance, and, where applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances; employer social security costs are included. The host receives research, training and networking costs plus management and indirect costs. The 2027 indicative budget is about €330M for European Fellowships and €58M for Global Fellowships. I couldn't confirm the exact monthly rates from official pages in this search; they are in the MSCA Work Programme 2026–2027.
